newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislature debates $511 mln prison bonds.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislature debates $511 mln prison bonds.

text.p: A California legislative panel on Tuesday will vote on a plan to issue more than $511 million of bonds to build two new state prisons.

The state Assembly Committee on Public Safety will consider Assembly Bill 1264, which would authorize the state to build a 2,000 cell prison in Kern County and a 2,500 cell prison and prison processing center in San Diego.

The bill would make $249.8 million available for construction of the Kern County facility and $261.4 million available for the San Diego projects. The prisons would be funded with lease-purchase bonds, state officials said.

The bill's author, Republican Assemblyman Charles Poochigian, said the new prisons are needed to ease overcrowding in state prisons, which currently hold 146,000 adult inmates. The prison population is expected to grow by an average of 10,500 inmates per year to 205,000 inmates by 2002.

Opponents of the prison proposal say lease-purchase bonds are more expensive for the state than general obligation bonds because lease-purchase bonds are not backed by the full taxing power of the state.
Opponents also contend that lease-purchase bonds rob the public of the right to approve major state bond issues. General obligation bonds, unlike lease-purchase bonds, require voter approval.

California's use of lease-purchase bonds has skyrocketed in recent years. Debt service on lease-purchase bonds has grown from 13 percent to 21 percent of total state debt service since 1991, according to recent state report.
